subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the inverse function of f(x) = log₂x.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.80 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 92.2. The book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages (unlike its LAQ/SAQ pages): the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Appearance years are the book's, board-split. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would invert log base two of x — the rewrite you use, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite as a power
steps.margin_note: One mark. Undo a logarithm by writing it in exponent form — the definition of a log is all you need.

recall.must_convey: That log₂x = y is rewritten by the definition of a logarithm as x = 2 to the power y.
accept: log base two of x equals y means x equals two to the power y
rewrite the log in exponential form to get x is two to the y
by the definition of a logarithm x equals two power y
log form ni exponent form lo rasthe x equals two power y
convert the logarithm to index form

steps.why: A logarithm and a power say the same thing two ways. Rewriting is not a calculation — it is the definition, and it is the whole method.
common_mistakes: Writing x = y², swapping the base and the exponent.
Trying to divide by log 2 instead of rewriting.

steps.label: Write the inverse
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the finished function, renamed in x.

recall.must_convey: That f⁻¹(x) = 2ˣ — the exponential with the same base as the logarithm.
accept: f inverse of x is two to the power x
the inverse is two power x
f inverse ante two power x
the answer is 2 to the x

steps.why: This is the previous question read backwards: the inverse of a logarithm is the exponential with the same base.
common_mistakes: Changing the base to e or 10.
